hero.title: Welcome to the CriptEnv Documentation
hero.subtitle: Everything you need to manage your secrets with military-grade security — from the CLI to the dashboard, from the API to CI/CD integrations.

whatIs.title: What is CriptEnv?
whatIs.paragraph1: CriptEnv is an open-source secrets management platform with a Zero-Knowledge architecture. An alternative to Doppler and Infisical, it lets developers and teams manage environment variables, API keys and sensitive credentials with end-to-end encryption.
whatIs.paragraph2: All secrets are encrypted 100% client-side with AES-256-GCM. The server never receives plaintext data — even with full access to the database, it is impossible to decrypt your credentials.

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-Knowledge
zeroKnowledge.description: Secrets are encrypted 100% client-side. The server stores only ciphertext — it never sees your real data.

consistent.title: Consistent
consistent.description: CLI and API share the same semantics. What you do in the terminal you can do over HTTP and vice versa.

secureByDefault.title: Secure by default
secureByDefault.description: AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-HKDF. No plaintext in logs, no token exposure, no data compromise.

concepts.title: Core Concepts
concepts.subtitle: Understand how projects, environments, vaults and the remote CLI connect to protect secrets end to end.
concepts.zeroKnowledgeCallout: CriptEnv is zero-knowledge: secrets are encrypted on the client and the server stores only encrypted blobs.

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-Knowledge
zeroKnowledge.description: All encryption happens on your device. The API never receives plaintext secrets or the project's Vault password.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Projects group related secrets and have their own Vault password to protect your data.

environments.title: Environments
environments.description: Environments separate configuration by stage, such as development, staging and production.

remoteVault.title: Remote Vault
remoteVault.description: The remote vault is the source of truth. It stores encrypted blobs and stays in sync across CLI, web and team.

vaultPassword.title: Vault Password
vaultPassword.description: Project password used only on the client to derive keys, decrypt in memory and prove vault access.

importExport.title: Import/Export
importExport.description: Push imports .env files into the remote vault. Pull exports remote secrets to local files.

howItWorks.title: Zero-Knowledge — How does it work?
howItWorks.step1: The CLI reads the project Vault password via prompt or CRIPTENV_VAULT_PASSWORD.
howItWorks.step2: The environment key is derived locally with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and HKDF.
howItWorks.step3: Secrets are encrypted or decrypted in memory with AES-256-GCM.
howItWorks.step4: The API receives only ciphertext, IV, auth tag, checksum and metadata.

concepts.vaultPasswordLostTip: If the project's Vault password is lost, that project's encrypted secrets cannot be recovered by the server.

projects.title: Projects and Environments
projects.text: Projects are collaboration namespaces. Environments isolate values by stage without mixing production, staging and development.

remoteCli.title: CLI as a Remote Terminal
remoteCli.text: The CLI does not keep a local secrets vault as its main flow. It resolves project and environment through the API, downloads encrypted blobs, operates in memory and sends the new encrypted blobs back.
